card: Uses mocktime in functional test p2p_tx_privacy.py to avoid flakiness from unbounded random inbound transaction announcement delays. The test previously relied on a 60-second real-time timeout, causing sporadic failures when Poisson delays exceeded the threshold. The author verified that advancing mocktime resolves a forced 12-minute delay in 1 second while maintaining regression detection. Addresses an instance of timeout flakiness tracked under issue #19732.
evidence: PR description: "`p2p_tx_privacy.py` waits 60 seconds for tx2's announcement but the node holds announcements behind a random delay that has no upper bound. An unlucky draw fails the test even though the node behaved as expected"

PR description verification: under a reproduction patch pinning NextInvToInbounds delay to 12 minutes, master fails after 60 seconds while the PR branch passes in 1 second and still catches regressions when net_processing guards are disabled
problem: The functional test p2p_tx_privacy.py waits 60 seconds in real time for a transaction announcement that is subject to an unbounded random delay. Unlucky random draws cause false-positive test timeouts on CI.

risk.why: A mistake would only cause test failures or false positives in the p2p_tx_privacy functional test.

scope_notes: A small test-only fix (+7/-0 in one file) addressing an instance of #19732.
summary: Freezes mocktime before peers connect in p2p_tx_privacy.py and advances it after queuing a transaction. This flushes outbound transaction announcements deterministically without waiting on real-time Poisson delays.
uncertainties: Diff was not provided in metadata, though the commit message and PR description clearly detail the 7-line test adjustment.
